## Extraction ledger — COMPLETE. Closing.

Every FAIL, PARTIAL and checklist-maintenance item extracted; all four premises re-verified live on `origin/main`, zero already-fixed, zero duplicates.

| Run item | Finding | Card | Lane |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `surface-matrix` c6 (FAIL) | `/i18n/locales` advertises 4 locales when the app declared 2 — `loadTranslations()` reads `defaultLocale` only and never narrows to `supportedLocales`, while each platform plugin pushes its own 4-locale bundle | #7679 | `domain:cli` |
| `studio-follows-app-locale` (PARTIAL) | date formatter half-localized — past relative forms localize, future forms and absolute timestamps stay `en-US` | objectstack-ai/objectui#4272 | objectui |
| `build-gates-hold` (PARTIAL) | the bundles gate reports a stale-dist **prerequisite** failure as a **content** verdict ("1 bundle problem(s)"), where its sibling coverage gate correctly refuses to judge | #7681 | `domain:devx` |
| `notification-localized-and-clears` c0/c4 (PARTIAL) | the clauses assume a per-recipient localized notification title — a capability the spec **retired** (`notifications` is a retired translation group; #3403 moved them to app-authored flows) | #7684 | `domain:devx` |
| Checklist maintenance ×3 | step-4 is a no-op as written (perturb a bundle **key**, not a value); `_sections` has no addressable surface; `emptyState` unauthored; c1 should allow the frozen untranslated debt | #7686 | `domain:devx` |

The PASS item (`strict-translation-key-rejection`, 20/20 rejections across both doors) produced no cards.

### Two notes worth carrying

**#4272's root cause was located beyond what the run stated.** The run observed the symptom; the extraction traced it to objectui `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` — `formatDateTime` (L551-563) takes no locale and calls `toLocaleDateString(undefined, …)`, which is why absolute timestamps render `en-US`, and `formatRelativeDays`'s future path never threads the app locale.

**#7681 is a gate-honesty defect, not the stale dist.** The `packages/spec/dist` staleness in this checkout is a build artifact, not the bug. The bug is that `looksLikeMissingCliCommand` only matches "command not found", so a stale-dist export mismatch falls through to `broken.push('extract failed')` and is reported as a content verdict — while the coverage gate handles the identical cause correctly ("Nothing was compared… the baseline was left exactly as committed", the #6033/#5862 honesty). #5217 added the CLI-case classifier only; this is its uncovered sibling.

Provenance: maintainer standing rule that every QA problem becomes an issue; run records close at extraction, same exit as #7514/#7463/#7627.
